title: Elasticity: a spring, stress and strain (স্থিতিস্থাপকতা)
placement: Book pages 147–148, topic 5.5 (স্থিতিস্থাপকতা): next to the paragraphs on বিকৃতি, পীড়ন, চিত্র ৫.১১ (a rod stretched by a weight W, tension T) and the box with হুকের সূত্র (পীড়ন ∝ বিকৃতি).
description: Elasticity (pages 147–148, topic 5.5) in a warm workshop: an old red-brick wall, a deep blue pegboard of tools and an oak bench, with a heavy lab stand from which a polished steel spring hangs (L₀ = 20 cm), a wooden metre rule reading its length L from the top hook, a hanger with a pointer, and brass slotted weights of 1 N each waiting on a block. One tap hangs a weight: it slides onto the hanger and the spring bounces and settles; a red line marks the stretch x beside the dark L₀ line, a bold orange arrow is the restoring force (টান T) in the spring and a purple one the weight W, the same length. Beside it a পীড়ন–বিকৃতি graph gets a point for every load. One weight gives x = 2 cm, two give 4 cm: twice the force, twice the strain, so পীড়ন ∝ বিকৃতি (Hooke's law), and the panel works out বিকৃতি = (L − L₀)/L₀ (no unit), পীড়ন = F/A on the wire's cross-section (A = 10 mm²) in Pa, and their constant ratio, live with Bangla digits. Weights off: the spring returns to L₀ (elasticity). Past 4 N, the elastic limit, it gives way: 5 weights stretch it 13 cm, not 10; the graph bends (hatched 'within the limit' and dotted 'past the limit' bands, named in the graph's key in the panel); with the weights off it stays 7 cm longer, its coils apart, and the graph shows the permanent set (স্থায়ী বিকৃতি). The rule grows in the book's words to Hooke's law and Young's modulus; a quiet button takes a new spring. Test tab: 5 questions (the strain from the rule, the stress from the weights, x for n weights, the elastic limit from the graph, why the spring stayed long), every wrong choice a real mistake with its own note. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
